entries.description:
Get comments for a specific Confluence page.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    page_id: Confluence page ID.

Returns:
    JSON string representing a list of comment objects.

page_id.description: Confluence page ID (numeric ID, can be parsed from URL, e.g. from 'https://example.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TEAM/pages/123456789/Page+Title' -> '123456789')

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_page
entries.description:
Get content of a specific Confluence page by its ID, or by its title and space key.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    page_id: Confluence page ID. If provided, 'title' and 'space_key' are ignored.
    title: The exact title of the page. Must be used with 'space_key'.
    space_key: The key of the space. Must be used with 'title'.
    include_metadata: Whether to include page metadata.
    convert_to_markdown: Convert content to markdown (true) or keep raw HTML (false).

Returns:
    JSON string representing the page content and/or metadata, or an error if not found or parameters are invalid.

page_id.description: Confluence page ID (numeric ID, can be found in the page URL). For example, in the URL 'https://example.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TEAM/pages/123456789/Page+Title', the page ID is '123456789'. Provide this OR both 'title' and 'space_key'. If page_id is provided, title and space_key will be ignored.

title.description: The exact title of the Confluence page. Use this with 'space_key' if 'page_id' is not known.

space_key.description: The key of the Confluence space where the page resides (e.g., 'DEV', 'TEAM'). Required if using 'title'.

include_metadata.description: Whether to include page metadata such as creation date, last update, version, and labels.

convert_to_markdown.description: Whether to convert page to markdown (true) or keep it in raw HTML format (false). Raw HTML can reveal macros (like dates) not visible in markdown, but CAUTION: using HTML significantly increases token usage in AI responses.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_search
entries.description:
Search Confluence content using simple terms or CQL.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    query: Search query - can be simple text or a CQL query string.
    limit: Maximum number of results (1-50).
    spaces_filter: Comma-separated list of space keys to filter by.

Returns:
    JSON string representing a list of simplified Confluence page objects.

query.description:
Search query - can be either a simple text (e.g. 'project documentation') or a CQL query string. Simple queries use 'siteSearch' by default, to mimic the WebUI search, with an automatic fallback to 'text' search if not supported. Examples of CQL:
- Basic search: 'type=page AND space=DEV'
- Personal space search: 'space="~username"' (note: personal space keys starting with ~ must be quoted)
- Search by title: 'title~"Meeting Notes"'
- Use siteSearch: 'siteSearch ~ "important concept"'
- Use text search: 'text ~ "important concept"'
- Recent content: 'created >= "2023-01-01"'
- Content with specific label: 'label=documentation'
- Recently modified content: 'lastModified > startOfMonth("-1M")'
- Content modified this year: 'creator = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfYear()'
- Content you contributed to recently: 'contributor = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfWeek()'
- Content watched by user: 'watcher = "user@domain.com" AND type = page'
- Exact phrase in content: 'text ~ "\"Urgent Review Required\"" AND label = "pending-approval"'
- Title wildcards: 'title ~ "Minutes*" AND (space = "HR" OR space = "Marketing")'
Note: Special identifiers need proper quoting in CQL: personal space keys (e.g., "~username"), reserved words, numeric IDs, and identifiers with special characters.

spaces_filter.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of space keys to filter results by. Overrides the environment variable CONFLUENCE_SPACES_FILTER if provided. Use empty string to disable filtering.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue
entries.description:
Get details of a specific Jira issue including its Epic links and relationship information.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    issue_key: Jira issue key.
    fields: Comma-separated list of fields to return (e.g., 'summary,status,customfield_10010'), a single field as a string (e.g., 'duedate'), '*all' for all fields, or omitted for essentials.
    expand: Optional fields to expand.
    comment_limit: Maximum number of comments.
    properties: Issue properties to return.
    update_history: Whether to update issue view history.

Returns:
    JSON string representing the Jira issue object.

Raises:
    ValueError: If the Jira client is not configured or available.

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of fields to return (e.g., 'summary,status,customfield_10010'). You may also provide a single field as a string (e.g., 'duedate'). Use '*all' for all fields (including custom fields), or omit for essential fields only.

expand.description: (Optional) Fields to expand. Examples: 'renderedFields' (for rendered content), 'transitions' (for available status transitions), 'changelog' (for history)

comment_limit.description: Maximum number of comments to include (0 or null for no comments)

properties.description: (Optional) A comma-separated list of issue properties to return

update_history.description: Whether to update the issue view history for the requesting user

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_search
entries.description:
Search Jira issues using JQL (Jira Query Language).

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    jql: JQL query string.
    fields: Comma-separated fields to return.
    limit: Maximum number of results.
    start_at: Starting index for pagination.
    projects_filter: Comma-separated list of project keys to filter by.
    expand: Optional fields to expand.
    page_token: Pagination token from a previous search result (Cloud only).

Returns:
    JSON string representing the search results including pagination info.

jql.description:
JQL query string (Jira Query Language). Examples:
- Find Epics: "issuetype = Epic AND project = PROJ"
- Find issues in Epic: "parent = PROJ-123"
- Find by status: "status = 'In Progress' AND project = PROJ"
- Find by assignee: "assignee = currentUser()"
- Find recently updated: "updated >= -7d AND project = PROJ"
- Find by label: "labels = frontend AND project = PROJ"
- Find by priority: "priority = High AND project = PROJ"

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated fields to return in the results. Use '*all' for all fields, or specify individual fields like 'summary,status,assignee,priority'

projects_filter.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of project keys to filter results by. Overrides the environment variable JIRA_PROJECTS_FILTER if provided.

page_token.description: (Optional) Pagination token from a previous search result. Cloud only — Server/DC uses start_at for pagination.

30 | 1. Problem Statement
31 | --------------------
32 | 
33 | ### 1.1 Context
34 | 
35 | The Zimmermann storefront serves a VIC (Very Important Customer) segment that has access to exclusive products not available to general customers. SFCC has no native mechanism to restrict product visibility at the customer group level — all products are visible to all users regardless of segment. There are 6–8 VIC Exclusive styles per season on average, and they routinely graduate to general availability, so the flag must be reversible.
36 | 
37 | ### 1.2 Problem
38 | 
39 | Site Merchandisers have no way to flag a product as VIC Exclusive in Business Manager. Without this, VIC Exclusive products are either surfaced to all customers in browse and search (undermining the exclusivity proposition) or must be withheld from the catalogue entirely (a merchandising limitation). There is no per-product visibility gate tied to customer group membership.
40 | 
41 | ### 1.3 Scope Framing — Suppression, Not Access Control
42 | 
43 | This section is the load-bearing framing for the whole document. In v0.3 it also carries the justification for accepting a client-side enforcement point, so it is worth reading before §3.
44 | 
45 | AC5 and AC6 require the product's PDP *and* the VIC Exclusive PLP to be fully accessible — and the product purchasable — by **any** customer holding the URL, regardless of customer group or login state. SFCC-303 is therefore a **merchandising suppression** story: hide VIC Exclusive products from general browse, search and crawlers, while leaving them open to anyone who has the link.
46 | 
47 | It follows that suppression does **not** need to be tamper-resistant. A customer who strips a refinement parameter gains access to something they were already entitled to view and buy. There is no confidentiality boundary to defend here. Genuine gating is deliberately deferred: purchase restriction is [SFCC-628](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-628) and private-marketing-URL access is [SFCC-629](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-629), both currently To Do.
48 | 
49 | Two consequences follow, and both are load-bearing later in this document:
50 | 
51 | * A client-side enforcement point is acceptable (§4.2). This is what makes the v0.3 recommendation viable at all — under the v0.1 gated reading it would have been unacceptable.
52 | * On any error or indeterminate state, the correct behaviour is to **fail open** (§5.4). Wrongly hiding general catalogue from a real shopper is a worse outcome than showing an openly-purchasable VIC product.
53 | 
54 | v0.1 of this document was written against the opposite (gated) interpretation and specified a PDP controller guard returning HTTP 404 to non-VIC customers. That guard is withdrawn — under the current ACs it would be a defect, not a feature. See §8 for the decision trail.
55 |

=== AC table 58-73 ===
58 | | **AC** | **Criterion** |
59 | | --- | --- |
60 | | AC1 | A Site Merchandiser can set `isVICExclusive` on a product in Business Manager and have it take effect on the next search index, with no developer involvement and no republishing or recreation of the product. |
61 | | AC2 | A product flagged `isVICExclusive = true` is not displayed in any category or PLP listing to a customer outside the VIC customer group. |
62 | | AC3 | The same product does not appear in site search results for a non-VIC customer, and does not contribute to any refinement counts. |
63 | | AC4 | A logged-in VIC customer sees the product in listings and search results as normal, with the VIC Exclusive badge per [SFCC-225](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-225). |
64 | | AC5 | **Any** customer navigating directly to the product PDP URL — regardless of customer group or login state — sees the PDP in full and can add to cart and purchase. |
65 | | AC6 | **Any** customer navigating directly to the VIC Exclusive PLP URL sees the PLP in full, and can add to cart and purchase from it. |
66 | | AC7 | Setting the flag back to false returns the product to normal listing and search behaviour for all customers on the next index. |
67 | | AC8 | The product's PDP is not indexed by search engines, and the product is not included in the Google Shopping feed. |

=== cart.md VIC section ===
## 9. Exclusive / VIP Products (CAI-046 – CAI-047, CRM-162 – CRM-164)

- Exclusive/VIP items are **visible only to eligible customer groups**; customer group membership is managed via Omneo and configured in SFCC Business Manager (CAI-046)
- Ineligible customers cannot see these items in search or PLP (CAI-047)
- A **private marketing URL** grants access to exclusive VIC products without requiring login or customer group assignment at browse time — but purchase is still restricted to the eligible group (CRM-162)
- **VIC Exclusive tag** displayed on PLP tile and PDP for eligible customers

---

## 10. Back-in-Stock Notifications (OM-033 – OM-034)

- Customer captures email on OOS product; the notify-me email and product details are submitted to **Emarsys** (CAI-029)
- Back-in-stock email sent to the first configurable-N customers on a FIFO basis when stock returns above buffer
- **No loyalty tier prioritisation** — strictly FIFO
- Guest capture timing is subject to the Omneo guest record creation open item (see AGENTS.md "Unresolved Dependencies")

---

## 11. No-Split Orders (CFD-033, CAI-033)

- No order splitting — all items in an order are delivered to the same address
- Customer is informed post-purchase if items ship in multiple parcels (via Narvar)

---

## 12. Open Items

- **CAI-005 — Recommendation engine for mini-cart carousel not confirmed.** The requirement text now reads "powered by SFCC Einstein (or Athos Commerce pending search platform decision)", but the row's open comment "Search / reccomendation engine not confirmed" persists and RJ adds "It is 99% likely we will move away from Athos". Treat platform (Einstein vs Athos Commerce) as undecided. **FLAG — cross-sheet contradiction:** Third_Party_Integrations (Search and Recommendations / Salesforce Einstein) states the system "will use Salesforce Einstein for all search, merchandising and product recommendation functionality across all storefronts," which contradicts CAI-005 treating the engine as unconfirmed. Do not silently resolve — confirm with Zimmermann which sheet is authoritative.
- **CAI-023 — MuleSoft warehouse + boutique aggregation feasibility.** IC: "We had a requirement that for a SKU/size to be considered 'in stock' then it would take into account an aggregated view of warehouse & boutique stock... Will Mulesoft be able to do this?" SFCC OOTB does not aggregate; aggregation capability pending confirmation.
- **CAI-034 — Real-time cart→checkout inventory check requires new MuleSoft flow.** "Currently the Mulesoft does not exists for this, and will require a new MuleSoft flow. Otherwise, we will just use inventory feed." Behaviour desired/confirmed, build dependency open.
- **CAI-041 — Location-aware boutique fallback.** RJ: "We need to consider the users location and we could potentially serve inventory from a nearby boutique." Potential post-launch enhancement.
- **CAI-037/039 — Find in Boutique design marked Phase 2.** Requirement Confirmed; designs not yet available for go-live timing.
- **ENH-038 / ENH-039 — SFCC-hosted wishlist being scoped (not confirmed).** Previously out of scope (wishlist to migrate to Omneo); both enhancements now flipped — ENH-038 (add OOS products to wishlist from PLP) Zimm response: *"ACN to size — wishlist in SFCC"*; ENH-039 (guest wishlist consolidating on login) Zimm response: *"ACN to size"* / *"To be sized"*. A SFCC-hosted wishlist for go-live is being sized but not confirmed. The Move-to-Wishlist behaviour (CAI-004/008) depends on whether the wishlist ultimately lives in SFCC vs Omneo (cf. ENH-040, which logs the SFCC→Omneo migration as a separate enhancement). Both still status "Under Review" — confirm hosting platform and go-live scope with Zimmermann before build.

# D. VIP / exclusive-access spec

**There IS a VIC Exclusive spec set — but the private-marketing-URL mechanism itself is NOT specified anywhere.** That distinction is the finding.

### What exists

**1. Requirement statement — page 302022672, "04.1.11 Customers, Account, CRM Sync"** (columns: `Req ID | Functional Area | Sub-Functional Area | Requirement | Owner | Storefront | Config/Custom | Status | Comments | User Story Link`):

> | **CRM-162** | Customers, Account & CRM Sync & Wishlist | My Account - Loyalty Page (New & Legacy Programme) | "**The system will support a private marketing URL that grants access to exclusive VIC products without requiring the customer to be logged in or assigned to a customer group**" | **Accenture** | ALL | **Custom** | Confirmed | *(comments empty)* |

> | **CRM-164** | … | "The system will restrict purchase of exclusive VIC products to customers assigned to an eligible customer group" | Accenture | ALL | **Custom** | Confirmed |

Note the classification: **Owner = Accenture, Config/Custom = Custom.** The confirmed requirements register does *not* treat this as configuration or platform-native.

**2. Page 302415874, "04.1.5 Cart and Inventory"** — the Cart-epic "Exclusive Access" rows. Both **Custom**, **Confirmed**, no comments, and **neither mentions a URL**:

> | CAI-046 | Exclusive Access | "The system will surface and make available exclusive/restricted items to customers in the eligible VIP customer group, based on customer group membership managed via Omneo and configured in SFCC Business Manager.'" |
> | CAI-047 | Exclusive Access | "The system will restrict visibility of exclusive/restricted items to eligible VIP customers only. These items will not be surfaced in search results or on the PLP for customers outside the eligible customer group." |

**3. Page 482345007, "04.4.6 VIC Exclusive — Merchandiser Working Guide"** — the closest thing to a mechanism statement anywhere:

> "**The VIC Exclusive landing page is a public-facing page accessible via a private token-based URL ([SFCC-629](…/browse/SFCC-629)). Customers do not need to be logged in or assigned to the VIC customer group to access it via this URL.**"
> "The landing page links out to each season's VIC Exclusive PLP. To add or update a season link: 1. Navigate to the VIC Exclusive landing page configuration in **Contentful** 2. Add or update the link pointing to the relevant season category PLP URL … 3. Publish the entry"

That is the whole of it. It names a **token-based URL** and a Contentful-configured landing page, and says nothing about how the token is minted, validated, scoped, expired, or distributed.

**4. Page 407666693, "TSD: VIC Exclusive Product Visibility" (TSD-SFCC-303, v0.6 Draft)** — explicitly **excludes** the mechanism:

> Related Jira: "SFCC-303 (this story) · SFCC-628 (purchase restriction — **out of scope**) · **SFCC-629 (private marketing URL — out of scope)** · SFCC-225 (product badges…)"
> §1.3: "Genuine gating is deliberately deferred: purchase restriction is SFCC-628 and **private-marketing-URL access is SFCC-629, both currently To Do**."

The TSD also records a decision that bears directly on the enhancement's premise:

> "3 Sep 2026 | Jasmijn Tsang | Products cannot be gated to VIC members while also letting VIC customers view them without logging in | Mixed gating would expose the products to anyone holding the URL regardless, so the two requirements are mutually exclusive. Forced an explicit choice."
> "4 Sep 2026 | Dani Rivett, relaying Courtney / Rebecca / CRM team | **Ungated experience for Spring 27** — products hidden from non-VIC clients but accessible via direct URL. Fully gated experience de-prioritised, to roll out later."

And it flags an unresolved PRD conflict, Open Decision #1: whether AC5's "can be added to cart and purchased" holds "against `cart.md` §9 / CRM-162, which still states purchase is restricted to the eligible customer group."

### NOT FOUND — explicit negatives

- **No spec page for the private-URL mechanism exists.** Searched `VIP exclusive product`, `private marketing URL`, `customer group exclusive access no login required`, `VIC customers loyalty exclusive access token`, `source code campaign`. Nothing defines token generation, validation, lifetime, revocation, or delivery.
- **No Zimmermann doc names SFCC source code groups or a `sourceCode` URL parameter as this mechanism.** The only occurrence of the term anywhere in the space is on page **344883203 "04.3.1 BM User Roles & Permissions Matrix"**, where "Source Code Groups" appears solely as a line item in a BM permission list ("…Promotions, A/B Tests, Content Slots, Coupons, **Source Code Groups**, Active Data, Stores, Gift Certificates, Import & Export Online Marketing, Consent Management, Notifications"). That is a role-permission listing, not a design. TSD-SFCC-303 contains **zero** occurrences of "source code", "sourceCode", or "campaign".
- The `sourceCode` hypothesis is therefore **your inference, not the project's** — nothing in Confluence or Jira corroborates it.

### The "out of the box" claim — FOUND, and unanswered

It is recorded, but in **Jira, not Confluence** — verbatim from SFCC-155's own description (see §F):

> "Accenture Additional Notes: Please provide some more information on what the private marketing URL is that you are looking for? E.g. what does the link lead to, does the customer need to be logged-in (and content based on customer group for example), or no log in - this would be difficult to implement/high effort
> **Zimm Response: Salesforce confirmed this is out of the box functionality - customer receives link via email to gain exclusive access, no login required**
> **Accenture Notes: What is the OOTB behaviour?**"

The Accenture follow-up question **"What is the OOTB behaviour?" was never answered** — SFCC-155 has zero comments, and no Confluence page addresses it. Meanwhile the confirmed requirements register (CRM-162) classifies the same requirement as **Custom / Accenture**, and SFCC-629's own description calls it **"SFCC Custom"**. Those two positions contradict each other and the contradiction is unresolved on the record.

### Duplicate-scope flag *(labelled inference)*

SFCC-155 (ENH-027, epic **Cart**, enhancement, sized FED 1 / BED 1, "Approved", consuming capacity) and **SFCC-629** (epic SFCC-16 **Customer Account & CRM**, label **CRM-162**, Squad-A, To Do, unassigned, unsized) appear to be **the same requirement counted twice** — SFCC-155's description is the ENH-027 restatement of CRM-162, and SFCC-629 carries CRM-162 as its label. There is **no Jira link between them** (SFCC-155 has no issuelinks; SFCC-629 links only to SFCC-303 as "relates to"). I have not found a document that reconciles the two, so treat this as inference, not established fact.

**Important:** RRC-004 — the requirement that actually governs the returns link on the order detail page — contains **no conditional-display rule at all**. The whole of 04.1.3 contains **no time window**, **no 15-day rule, no 28-day rule, and no mention of a delivery date**. ### NOT FOUND — explicit negatives

- **The 28-day fallback rule appears in NO Confluence page.** Exact-phrase CQL `text ~ "\"28 days\"" AND type = page` in space SFCC returned **`[]`**. It exists only in the SFCC-142 Jira description's Zimm Response (§F) and in this repo's own local docs (`.docs/prd/returns.md:60`, `.docs/memory/projectState.md:194`), both of which cite ENH-014 as their source.

Page 303431681 names the MuleSoft returns API (RRC-007: `GET /api/returns?customer_id=`) but not a delivery date. The only record of the dependency is the SFCC-142 Zimm Response itself: "This second requirement is third party dependent - we need the delivery date passed back via MuleSoft" — i.e. the dependency is **asserted by the requester and nowhere accepted by the integration stream**.
- The eligibility open question is still live on both INT matrices: "Confirm return eligibility window per market" (256442388) and "Confirm return eligibility rules per market (window in days).
